esto|pron|.note: s1: replace '¿Qué es [esto]?' / 'What is this?' with '¿Para qué sirve [esto]?' / 'What is this for?' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'qué'.

algo|pron|.note: s4: replace 'Estoy [algo] cansado.' / 'I'm a bit tired.' with '¿Sabes [algo] de ella?' / 'Do you know anything about her?' because s4 uses algo as an adverb ('a bit'), not the glossed pronoun; the new line also covers the 'anything' sense. Keep the note about 'algo cansado'.

bueno|adj|.note: s2: replace 'Es una [buena] idea.' / 'It's a good idea.' with 'La comida está muy [buena].' / 'The food is very good.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'un'.

cómo|adv|.note: s1: replace '¿[Cómo] estás?' / 'How are you?' with '¿[Cómo] vas al trabajo?' / 'How do you get to work?' (duplicates a sentence of 'estar'); s2: replace '¿[Cómo] te llamas?' / 'What's your name?' with '¿[Cómo] se dice «gracias» en inglés?' / 'How do you say "gracias" in English?' (duplicates a sentence of 'te').

o|conj|.note: s3: cloze is wrong: it marks the final letter of 'Llego' ('Lleg[o]'). The cloze must be the standalone word: 'Llego en dos [o] tres días.' (set the cloze explicitly to the second whole-word 'o', not the first substring match).

hacer|verb|.note: s4: replace '¿Qué estás [haciendo]?' / 'What are you doing?' with 'Esta noche [hago] yo la cena.' / 'I'm making dinner tonight.' because s4 has the same meaning and translation as s1, and no sentence shows the 'to make' sense of the gloss.

gracias|interj|.note: s2: replace '[Gracias] por todo.' / 'Thanks for everything.' with '[Gracias] por tu ayuda.' / 'Thanks for your help.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'por'.

creer|verb|.note: s1: replace '[Creo] que sí.' / 'I think so.' with '[Creo] que va a llover.' / 'I think it's going to rain.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'sí' (keep the note).

hola|interj|.note: s3: replace 'Dile [hola] de mi parte.' / 'Say hi to him for me.' with '[Hola], ¿está Ana?' / 'Hello, is Ana there?' because 'decir hola de mi parte' is calqued from English (natives say 'Salúdalo de mi parte' / 'Dale saludos'), and 'dile' is not specifically 'him'.

casa|noun|.note: s1: replace 'Estoy en [casa].' / 'I'm at home.' with 'Los domingos me quedo en [casa].' / 'On Sundays I stay home.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'en'.

dos|num|.note: s1: replace 'Tengo [dos] hermanos.' / 'I have two brothers.' with 'Quiero [dos] cafés, por favor.' / 'I'd like two coffees, please.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'tener'.

favor|noun|.note: s1: replace 'Por [favor], ven aquí.' / 'Please come here.' with 'Por [favor], cierra la puerta.' / 'Please close the door.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'por'.

mí|pron|.note: s3: replace 'Habla de [mí].' / 'He's talking about me.' with 'Siempre habla de [mí].' / 'He's always talking about me.' because the bare 'Habla de mí' reads just as easily as the command 'Talk about me', and the fuller line is more natural.

también|adv|.note: s1: replace 'Yo [también].' / 'Me too.' with 'Mi hermano [también] viene.' / 'My brother is coming too.' because the original duplicates a sentence of 'yo'.

hombre|noun|.note: s1: replace 'Es un [hombre] muy bueno.' / 'He's a very good man.' with 'Mi abuelo era un [hombre] muy alto.' / 'My grandfather was a very tall man.' because it nearly repeats bueno s1 'Es un buen hombre.' (same sentence a few cards apart).

vida|noun|.note: s4: replace 'Los médicos salvan [vidas].' / 'Doctors save lives.' with 'Tenemos [vidas] muy diferentes.' / 'We have very different lives.' because s3 already uses 'salvar la vida' (no variety) and 'salvan' is flagged rare.

alguien|pron|.note: s1: replace '[Alguien] está en la puerta.' with 'Hay [alguien] en la puerta.' (translation unchanged: 'Someone is at the door.') because natives use 'hay' for an indefinite subject; 'Alguien está en…' sounds translated.

siempre|adv|.note: s2: replace 'Te querré para [siempre].' / 'I'll love you forever.' with 'Vamos a ser amigos para [siempre].' / 'We're going to be friends forever.' because 'querré' (irregular future) is rare and hard for beginners.

año|noun|.note: s2: replace 'Feliz [año] nuevo.' / 'Happy New Year.' with '¡Feliz [año] nuevo!' / 'Happy New Year!' because a greeting/wish needs exclamation marks (¡ !) in Spanish.

poco|det|.note: s1: replace 'Habla un [poco] más alto.' / 'Speak a little louder.' with 'Tengo [poco] dinero.' / 'I don't have much money.' because s1 and s4 both use adverbial 'un poco', not the glossed determiner; the new line shows masculine singular 'poco' before a noun.

mirar|verb|.note: s3: replace 'Me [miró] y sonrió.' / 'He looked at me and smiled.' with 'Nadie me [miró].' / 'Nobody looked at me.' because 'sonrió' is rare (outside top 10000) and distracts beginners.

pasar|verb|.note: s4: replace '¿Qué ha [pasado] aquí?' / 'What has happened here?' with '¿Me [pasas] la sal?' / 'Can you pass me the salt?' because s1, s2 and s4 are all 'what happened' questions, and no sentence shows the glossed 'to pass' sense.

mañana|noun|.note: s3: replace 'Por las [mañanas] corro.' / 'I run in the mornings.' with 'Trabajo por las [mañanas].' / 'I work in the mornings.' because 'corro' is flagged rare and the fronted word order is less neutral for beginners.

valer|verb|.note: s4: replace '[Valió] la pena.' / 'It was worth it.' with 'Antes esta casa [valía] mucho más.' / 'This house used to be worth much more.' because s3 and s4 repeat the same idiom 'valer la pena'; the new line adds the plain 'be worth' sense and the imperfect form.

lugar|noun|.note: s3: replace 'Hay [lugares] muy bonitos aquí.' / 'There are very nice places here.' with 'Me gusta visitar [lugares] nuevos.' / 'I like visiting new places.' because s3 repeats s1's 'muy bonito' framing (no variety of context).

nuestro|det|.note: s2 translation: replace 'Our house is near.' with 'Our house is nearby.' because bare 'is near' is unnatural English.

luego|adv|.note: s1: replace '[Luego] te llamo.' / 'I'll call you later.' with 'Ahora no puedo, [luego] hablamos.' / 'I can't now, we'll talk later.' because it has the same meaning and translation as después s1 'Te llamo después.' (ambiguous cloze across cards); s2: replace 'Primero estudio y [luego] salgo.' / 'First I study and then I go out.' with 'Cenamos y [luego] vimos una película.' / 'We had dinner and then watched a movie.' because it mirrors después s3 'Primero comemos y después hablamos.'.
